title: Auto mode for Claude Code
description: Anthropic introduced a new 'auto mode' in Claude Code where Claude makes permission decisions on your behalf with safeguards. The safeguards use Claude Sonnet 4.6 as a classifier to review actions before they run, blocking actions that escalate beyond task scope or target untrusted infrastructure. The system has extensive default filters for allowed operations (like local file operations and read-only calls) and blocked operations (like git force push, downloading and executing external code). Simon Willison remains skeptical of prompt-based protections, preferring deterministic sandboxes for AI coding agents.
author: Simon Willison

title: Package Managers Need Cooldowns After LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack
description: Following the LiteLLM v1.82.8 supply chain attack that included a credential stealer, Simon Willison advocates for dependency cooldowns - only installing updated dependencies after they've been available for a few days. Major packaging tools now support this: pnpm, Yarn, Bun, Deno, uv, pip, and npm all have minimum release age features. The LiteLLM attack exploited stolen PyPI credentials from a Trivy vulnerability and would have harvested a vast array of credentials and secrets from developers' machines.
author: Simon Willison

title: Streaming Experts: Running Massive LLMs on Consumer Hardware
description: Dan Woods' 'streaming experts' technique allows running larger Mixture-of-Experts models on hardware without enough RAM by streaming necessary expert weights from SSD. Recent achievements include running Qwen3.5-397B-A17B in 48GB RAM, the 1 trillion parameter Kimi K2.5 model on a 96GB M2 Max MacBook Pro, and even running these models on an iPhone at 0.6 tokens/second. The technique continues to improve through autoresearch loops finding optimizations.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI-Assisted Coding is Exposing a Developer Divide
description: Les Orchard observes that AI-assisted coding is revealing a fundamental split among developers that was always present but less visible. Before AI, both 'craft-lovers' and 'make-it-go' developers appeared identical because they used the same workflow. Now there's a fork: let the machine write code and focus on directing what gets built, or hand-craft everything. This choice makes visible the underlying motivation for why people got into programming.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Les Orchard)

title: NYT Magazine: Coding After Coders - The End of Programming As We Know It
description: Clive Thompson's comprehensive piece in the New York Times Magazine interviewed 70+ software developers from major tech companies about AI-assisted development. Simon Willison is quoted on how programming has a unique advantage: code can be tested to verify correctness, unlike legal briefs or other AI-generated content. The piece captures the industry shift toward AI coding tools while noting that some developers lament the loss of hand-crafting code. Corporate dynamics may be suppressing honest discussion about this transition.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic Launches Code Review Tool to Check Flood of AI-Generated Code
description: Anthropic launched 'Code Review' in Claude Code, a multi-agent system that automatically analyzes AI-generated code and flags logic errors. The tool addresses the bottleneck in pull request reviews caused by dramatically increased code output from AI coding tools. Code Review uses multiple AI agents working in parallel to examine code from different perspectives, with a final agent aggregating and prioritizing findings. It focuses on logical errors rather than style, explains reasoning step-by-step, and labels issue severity with colors. Pricing is token-based at $15-25 per review on average.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: OpenAI Adds Open Source Tools to Help Developers Build for Teen Safety
description: OpenAI released a set of open-source prompts that developers can use to make their AI apps safer for teens. The policies work with OpenAI's gpt-oss-safeguard model but are designed as prompts to be compatible with other models. They address issues like graphic violence, sexual content, harmful body ideals, dangerous activities, romantic or violent roleplay, and age-restricted goods. Developed with Common Sense Media and everyone.ai, the prompts help translate safety goals into operational rules to avoid protection gaps, inconsistent enforcement, or overly broad filtering.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: Apple Overhauls App Developer Platform With 100 New Metrics
description: Apple announced a major update to App Store Connect, adding over 100 new metrics for tracking monetization, subscription data, and user behavior. The update provides first-party insights based on Apple's actual data rather than estimates from third-party services. New features include subscription reports exportable via API, cohort analysis for user behavior, peer group benchmarks for comparison, and up to seven simultaneous filters. The timing suggests Apple is working to ensure AI elevates rather than destroys its App Store ecosystem as AI agents become more capable.
author: Sarah Perez
